title: Negative group delay occurred in passive models of two partial adult worm electrical maps
abstract: We tested whether negative group delay can occur in passive circuit models of two partial adult C. elegans electrical maps. At uniform leak 0.1, 2 of 6702 qualifying unordered cell pairs in map 7 and 4 of 7946 in map 8 passed a negative-delay rule at three successive sampled frequencies. The rule used fixed DC and frequency response floors and a delay margin. Counts changed with leak, weights, grid spacing and response floors. Direct complex solves and phase derivatives checked selected cases. A three-cell passive triangle gives an exact example. Its impulse response is causal and nonnegative, as are those of the map models. Thus a negative finite-frequency phase derivative does not by itself require active signaling or a response before input onset. This is an exploratory model benchmark, not measured activity. Partial anatomy, assumed conductances and uniform physiology limit biological inference. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps support reproduction. External graph records are not bundled.

display.caption: Negative-delay pair shares across assumed leaks and weights, and across frequency at leak 0.1. Counts use dependent pairs from two fixed partial maps, not independent animal samples.
